OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing away of 
Kumari Nirmala Deshpande, a distinguished sitting Member of this House, on 1 st 
May, 2008 at the age of 79 years. 
Born at Nagpur, Maharashtra, in October, 1929, Kumari Deshpande has her education 
at the Nagpur University. She was conferred honorary doctorate by the Punjabi University, 
Patiala, University of Amravati, Maharashtra and Kashi Vidyapeeth, Varanasi. 
A true disciple of Vinoba Bhave, Kumari Deshpande joined his Bhoodan Yatra in 
1952 and walked more than 40,000 kilometres to propagate the ideology of non-violent 
revolution. She organised peace marches in the militancy-ridden States of Punjab and 
Jammu and Kashmir, and worked tirelessly for maintaining peace and communal harmony. 
She was also deeply involved in other efforts to bring about peace, especially, between 
India and Pakistan. 
Kumari Deshpande was associated with various social welfare organisations and served 
them in various capacities. She was the National President of the Akhil Bharat Rachnatmak 
Samaj, an organisation committed to peace and non-violence. She also served as the National 
President of the Harijan Sevak Sangh and as the Chairperson of the Association of People 
of Asia and India-Pakistan Forum of Parliamentarians. 
Kumari Deshpande has many publications to her credit. Apart from writing on religion 
and spirituality, Kumari Deshpande wrote a number of novels, plays and travelogues. She 
was the Editor of the fortnightly Nityanutan, published from Delhi and Maitri, a journal on 
service and spirituality. She also formed a forum of writers and artists names 'Sanjhi Virasat' 
to uphold India's tradition of composite culture and pluralism. 
A recipient of Padma Vibhushan and the Rajiv Gandhi Sadbhavana Puraskar, Kumari 
Deshpande won many laurels for her dedicated social service and efforts to promote communal 
harmony. 
A widely travelled person, Kumari Deshpande visited many countries in connection 
with the propagation of Gandhian thought. 
Kumari Deshpande was a Nominated Member of the Rajya Sabha from August, 1997 to 
August, 1999 and again from June, 2004 till her untimely demise. 
In the passing away of Kumari Nirmala Deshpande, the country has lost a renowned 
Gandhian and an eminent social activist.
